To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
homing pigeons exposed to Deepwater oil spill crude oil changed their flight performance and behavior.
Light external crude oil exposure of homing pigeons flying 161 km repeated flights resulted in increased flight duration, increased flight distance and reduced route efficiency.
homing pigeons exposed to a single low level oiling event exhibited flight performance and behavior changes that could negatively impact their migration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects that a low level oiling event has had on the behavior, physiology and flight performance of a surrogate migratory bird species.
the fate of migratory birds that were oiled by the DWH oil spill but did not perish as a direct result.
the effects of oil exposure on the flight performance of free-flying birds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of a low-level oiling event on flight performance and behavior were significant and that the effects on flight behavior were likely to be detrimental to long distance migratory birds.
our results suggest that oil spills can have negative consequences for birds migrating through the Gulf of Mexico.
the oil spill likely had a negative effect on migratory birds, and the effects of the spill may have lasted longer than previously thought.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
oiling events, even at very low levels, may have significant impacts on birds that are not immediately apparent, but can have long term effects on their fitness.
the oil spill may be a significant factor contributing to the mortality of migrating birds, and the long term effects of oiling on birds may be more significant than previously thought.
birds that survive an oiling event are likely to experience flight performance impairments that may affect the timing of migration and subsequent survival.
The main takeaway from our work is that
birds that are oiled, but survive, may be at a fitness disadvantage, and that the effects of oil spills on migratory birds are likely to be more complex than previously thought.
oil spills have the potential to cause significant flight impairment in free-flying birds.
even low level external oil contamination can have a negative effect on flight behavior and physiology, which may have long term effects on the survival and reproductive success of birds.
